title.value: SVRG meets AdaGrad: Painless Variance Reduction
title.justification: The title provided is the exact match from the paper details.
title.quote: Title: SVRG meets AdaGrad: Painless Variance Reduction

extractions.description: The paper introduces AdaSVRG, a variance-reduction method that combines SVRG with AdaGrad to adaptively determine step sizes in stochastic optimization without requiring problem-dependent constants. This method shows improved convergence and robustness in optimizing machine learning models, particularly with large datasets, by eliminating the need for tuning and efficiently transitioning between deterministic and stochastic optimization phases.

sustainable_development_is_central.justification: The central theme of the paper is on improving optimization algorithms (specifically SVRG) for machine learning rather than a direct contribution to sustainable development. It explores algorithm efficiency and robustness, targeted at better performance in the general domain of machine learning.
sustainable_development_is_central.quote: Variance reduction (VR) methods (Schmidt et al., 2017;... have proven to be an important class of algorithms for stochastic optimization.

primary_category.justification: The paper focuses on deep learning and optimization techniques, which do not have a direct or central focus on climate or ecological sustainable development issues.
primary_category.quote: Variance reduction (VR) methods for finite-sum minimization typically require the knowledge of problem-dependent constants... To address this, we use ideas from adaptive gradient methods to propose AdaSVRG.

secondary_categories.justification: Given that the primary focus is on algorithmic improvements for general ML applications rather than specific sustainable development areas, it lacks relevance as a secondary theme as well.
secondary_categories.quote: Variance reduction (VR) methods for finite-sum minimization...

primary_sub_category.justification: The paper does not provide content relevant to the sub-categories associated with climate or ecological sustainable development.
primary_sub_category.quote: To address this, we use ideas from adaptive gradient methods to propose AdaSVRG, which is a more-robust variant of SVRG, a common VR method.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: No content in the paper pertains to the predefined sub-categories related to sustainable development.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Next, we leverage the properties of AdaGrad to propose a heuristic that adaptively determines the length of each inner-loop in AdaSVRG.

applications.value: Optimization in large data machine learning models
applications.justification: The paper develops an advanced optimization technique that is particularly useful for machine learning model training on large datasets.
applications.quote: Via experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets, we validate the robustness and effectiveness of AdaSVRG, demonstrating its superior performance over standard and other 'tune-free' VR methods.
